source_text: Nam cum pronuntias, concupiscentiam carnis a principe tenebrarum in homine fuisse plantatam, eamque esse diaboli fruticem, ex se humanum genus quasi poma propria proferentem; absolute quidem proderis, quod non Deum, sed diabolum dicas hominum conditorem; quo dogmate impiissimo, et coniugiorum negotium, id est, genitalium admixtio, et caro cuncta damnatur.
pass_a_gloss: For when you pronounce that concupiscence of the flesh was planted in the human being by the prince of darkness, and that it is the devil's shrub, bringing forth from itself the human race as if its own fruits; you will indeed be absolutely betrayed, that you say not God but the devil is the founder of human beings; by which most impious dogma both the business of marriages, that is, the mixing of the genitals, and all flesh is damned.

lemmas.lexica: LS concupiscentia=eager desire; Blaise Christian usage often sexual desire vs nuptiae
LS conditor; Blaise God as maker from nothing

pass_b_english: For when you declare that the prince of darkness planted sexual desire in humanity, and that it is the devil’s shrub producing the human race from itself as its own fruit, you clearly betray yourself: you call the devil, rather than God, the creator of human beings. By this utterly impious doctrine both the business of marriage—that is, genital union—and all flesh are condemned.

choices.why: Julian distinguishes nuptiae from concupiscentia; do not flatten to 'lust' as a nature-sin substance.
Augustine's quoted claim that the unbaptized remain under the devil; keep the personal devil, not 'evil'.
rejected: under Satan (name not in the Latin here)

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
